'''Astros II''' ('''A'''rtillery '''S'''a'''T'''uration '''RO'''cket '''S'''ystem) is a self-propelled [[multiple rocket launcher]] produced in Brazil by the [[Avibras]] company. It features modular design and employs rockets with calibers ranging from 127 to 450&nbsp;mm (5–17.72 inches).  It was developed on the basis of a Tectran VBT-2028 6×6 all-terrain vehicle for enhanced mobility based on Mercedes-Benz 2028 truck chassis<ref name= ":0">{{Cite web |title=Astros 2020 MLRS: Brazils Industrial Investment in Precision Strike |url= http://www.defenseindustrydaily.com/astros-2020-brazil-moves-to-revive-avibras-07069/ |access-date= 2021-04-12 |website=Defense Industry Daily}}</ref> while later versions use [[Tatra 815-7]] chassis.

==Overview==
[[File:Operação_Formosa_2014_(15481886779).jpg|thumb|Astros II MK6 Brazilian Marine Corps.]]
A full Astros system includes 1 wheeled 4×4 Battalion level Command Vehicle (AV-VCC), which commands 3 batteries, and a series of 4×4 and 6×6 wheeled vehicles.<ref name=":0" /> Each battery consists of:<ref>{{cite web |last1=Castilho |first1=Pablo |title=A LOGÍSTICA NO GRUPO DE MÍSSEIS E FOGUETES EM OPERAÇÕES: UMA PROPOSTA DOUTRINÁRIA. |url=https://bdex.eb.mil.br/jspui/bitstream/123456789/3971/1/TCC_Castilho.pdf |website=Bibliotheca do Exercito |publisher=CENTRO DE INSTRUÇÃO DE ARTILHARIA DE MÍSSEIS E FOGUETES |access-date=7 June 2023}}</ref>
* 1 wheeled 4×4 Battery-level Command vehicle (AV-PCC)
* 1 wheeled 6×6 Radar Fire Control vehicle (AV-UCF)
* 6 wheeled 6×6 Universal Multiple Rocket Launchers vehicle (AV-LMU)
* 3 wheeled 6×6 Ammunition Resupply vehicles (AV-RMD)
* 1 wheeled 6×6 Field repair/workshop vehicle (AV-OFVE)
* 1 wheeled 4×4 Mobile Weather Station vehicle (AV-MET).

In the older version of the system, the [[Fire-control system|fire control]] vehicle were listed as optional vehicle in a battery.  The command vehicles and weather stations are recent additions, designed to improve overall system performance on newer versions. All vehicles are transportable in a C-130 Hercules.<ref name= ":0" /> The launcher is capable of firing rockets of different calibers armed with a range of warheads.<ref name=":1">{{cite web | work = Army technology | date = 2013-08-31 |url= http://www.army-technology.com/projects/astros/|title= Astros II Artillery Saturation Rocket System|access-date=28 December 2016 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130831184905/http://www.army-technology.com/projects/astros/ |archive-date= 31 August 2013|url-status=live}}</ref>

Each rocket resupply truck carries up to two complete reloads.

==Service history==
The Astros II artillery system entered service with the Brazilian Army in the early 1990s.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Bastos|first=Expedito Carlos Stephani|date=2021-12-13|title=40 anos do sistema de artilharia de foguetes brasileiro Avibras Astros II 1981 - 2021|url=https://www.ecsbdefesa.com.br/40-anos-do-sistema-de-artilharia-de-foguetes-brasileiro-avibras-astros-ii-1981-2021/|website=ECSB Defesa|access-date=2024-08-23}} p. 7.</ref> The system is battle proven, having been used in action by the Iraqi Army in the Gulf Wars.

In the 1980s, Avibrás sold an estimated 66 Astros II artillery systems to Iraq. Iraq also built the Sajeel-60 which is a license-built version of the Brazilian SS-60. Sixty Astros II were sold to [[Saudi Arabia]]<ref name = "autogenerated3">{{cite web |url= http://www.armyrecognition.com/moyen_orient/Saudi_Arabia/Index_Saudi_Arabia_army_ground_foces_military_equipment.htm|title=Military army ground forces equipment Saudi Arabian Army Forces |first= Alain|last= Servaes |access-date=28 December 2016 | work = Army recognition |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160303170358/http://www.armyrecognition.com/moyen_orient/Saudi_Arabia/Index_Saudi_Arabia_army_ground_foces_military_equipment.htm|archive-date=3 March 2016|url-status= live}}</ref> and an unspecified number sold to Bahrain and Qatar. Total sales of the Astros II between 1982 and 1987 reached US$1 billion. This fact made the Astros II multiple rocket launcher the most profitable weapon produced by Avibrás.<ref name= "autogenerated2">{{Cite web |url= http://www.uga.edu/cits/documents/pdf/BrazilXC.pdf |title= Export Controls In Brazil |access-date=2008-02-05 | publisher = UGA |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20060221211902/http://www.uga.edu/cits/documents/pdf/BrazilXC.pdf |archive-date=2006-02-21 |url-status= live}}</ref>

In the 1980s and early 1990s, Avibrás manufactured almost exclusively rockets and multiple-launch rocket systems (MLRS), such as the Astros II, in addition to developing antitank and antiship missiles. At its peak, Avibrás employed 6,000 people; later it would be reduced to 900 people in the early 1990s as the arms industry demand fell.  Even so, in the first Gulf War in 1991, the Astros II was successfully used by Saudi Arabia against Iraq.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/business/1525374.stm| publisher = BBC | work = News – Business | title = Cruise missiles 'Made in Brazil'|access-date=28 December 2016|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20080329022700/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/business/1525374.stm|archive-date=29 March 2008|url-status= live}}</ref> The Astros II system was also procured by [[Angola]] during the 1990s, for use against [[UNITA]] guerillas.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Arms Trade [Angola: Arms Trade a] |url=https://www.hrw.org/reports/archives/africa/ANGOLA94N.htm |access-date=2026-06-16 |website=www.hrw.org}}</ref>

==New generation==
[[File:Indonesian Army Astros MRLS firing a salvo 2017.jpg|thumb|Astros II Mk6 of Indonesian Army firing SS-09TS rocket.]]
The next step is an ambitious program, the Astros 2020 (Mk6), based on a 6×6 wheeled chassis.<ref name="Archived copy">{{Cite web |url=http://www.military-today.com/artillery/astros_iii.htm |title= Astros III |access-date=2017-12-03 | work = Military today |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20171208173524/http://www.military-today.com/artillery/astros_iii.htm |archive-date=2017-12-08 |url-status= usurped}}</ref> Being a new concept, it will require an estimated investment of R$1.2 billion, of which about US$210 million will be invested solely in development. It will be integrated with the cruise missile [[AVMT-300]] with 300-km range during the stage of testing and certification. It is said that the venture will, for example, enable the Army to integrate the Astros with defense anti-aircraft guns, paving the way for the utilization of common platforms, trucks, parts of electronic sensors and command vehicles.<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://economia.estadao.com.br/noticias/not_6638.htm |title= Governo torna-se sócio da Avibrás Aeroespecial |access-date= 2010-06-22 | last = Godói | first = Roberto | work = Estadão |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100610031356/http://economia.estadao.com.br/noticias/not_6638.htm |archive-date=2010-06-10 |url-status= live}}</ref>  The new MK6 system will use Tatra Trucks’ T815-790R39 6×6 and T815-7A0R59 4×4 trucks instead of the original Mercedes-Benz 2028A 6×6 truck. ASTROS 2020 offers several basic improvements including an improved armored cabin, modern digital communications and navigation systems, and a new tracking radar that replaces the AV-UCF's Contraves Fieldguard system.<ref name= ":0" /> The new tracking radar used by MK6 AV-UCF was later revealed to be the Fieldguard 3 Military Measurement System from Rheinmetall Air Defence.<ref>{{Cite web| publisher = Rheinmetall Defence | work = Archive | year = 2018 | title = Follow-up order from Brazil for Rheinmetall's Fieldguard 3 measurement system |url= https://www.rheinmetall-defence.com/en/rheinmetall_defence/public_relations/news/archiv/2018/aktuellesdetailansicht_8_20160.php |access-date=2021-04-12}}</ref> The Astros 2020 will also be equipped with a 180&nbsp;mm [[Global positioning system|GPS]]-guided rocket called the SS-AV-40G with a range of {{convert|40|km|mi|abbr=on}} and SS-150 newly developed rockets with a claimed maximum range of 150&nbsp;km. Four of them are carried.<ref name= "Archived copy"/> 36 Astros 2020 systems are to be acquired.<ref>[http://www.armyrecognition.com/december_2012_new_army_military_defence_industry/brazilian_army_will_continue_the_upgrade_program_of_its_rocket_launcher_systems_astros_2912122.html Brazilian army will continue to upgrade Astros rocket launchers] {{Webarchive|url= https://web.archive.org/web/20130102033812/http://www.armyrecognition.com/december_2012_new_army_military_defence_industry/brazilian_army_will_continue_the_upgrade_program_of_its_rocket_launcher_systems_astros_2912122.html |date=2013-01-02}}, Army recognition, December 29, 2012</ref>

==Rocket variants==
[[File:Astross MLRS in display during 2022 MAF's open day in RMAF Kuantan.jpg|thumb|Astros II in Malaysian Army digital camouflage.]]
* '''SS-09TS''' – fires 70&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 40
* '''SS-30''' – fires 127&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 32
* '''SS-40''' – fires 180&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 16
* '''SS-40G''' – fires 180&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 16 (GPS Guided)
* '''SS-60''' – fires 300&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 4
* '''SS-80''' – fires 300&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 4
* '''SS-80G''' – fires 300&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 4 (GPS Guided)
* '''SS-150''' – fires 450&nbsp;mm rockets – Loads 4 (GPS Guided)
* '''[[MANSUP]]''' – fires 330&nbsp;mm anti-ship missile – Loads 2<ref>{{cite web| url = https://www.defesaaereanaval.com.br/defesa/siatt-avanca-na-integracao-do-mansup-ao-sistema-astros | title = SIATT avança na integração do MANSUP ao Sistema ASTROS | website = Defesa Aérea e Naval | date = 1 October 2024 | language = pt }}</ref>
* '''[[AV-TM 300]]''' – fires 450&nbsp;mm cruise missile – Loads 2
* '''FOG MPM''' – fiber optics guided multi-purpose missile – anti-tank, anti-fortification and anti-helicopter missile
* '''FOG MLM''' – fiber optics guided multi-purpose missile

==Specifications==
[[File:Astros II MK6 and MTC-300 Cruise Missile.jpg|thumb|Astros II MK6 Brazilian Army launcing [[AV-TM 300]] .]]
[[File:Operação Atlas - 2025 74.jpg|thumb|Astros system fitted for MANSUP anti-ship missile.]]
[[File:Ministro da defesa Visita Fábrica da AVIBRAS (44828533281).jpg|thumb|FOG-MPM.]]
* Range in indirect fire mode<ref>{{Cite web |url= http://www.fas.org/man/dod-101/sys/land/row/astros.htm |title= Astros (Artillery SaTuration ROcket System) |access-date= 2006-06-27 | publisher = FAS |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20060421152921/http://fas.org/man/dod-101/sys/land/row/astros.htm |archive-date=2006-04-21 |url-status= live}}</ref> (first figure is minimum range):
** SS-09TS: 4–10&nbsp;km
** SS-30: 9–30&nbsp;km
** SS-40: 15–40&nbsp;km
** SS-40G: 15–40&nbsp;km
** SS-60: 20–60&nbsp;km
** SS-80: 22–90&nbsp;km
** SS-80G: 22–90&nbsp;km
** SS-150: 29–150&nbsp;km
** [[MANSUP]]: 70–200&nbsp;km
** [[AV-TM 300]]: 30–300&nbsp;km
** FOG MPM: 5–60&nbsp;km
* Armour: classified. Probably light composite to give protection against small-arms fire.
* Armament: one battery of 2, 4, 16 or 32 rocket-launcher tubes
* Performance:
** fording 1.1 m
** vertical obstacle 1 m
** trench 2.29 m
* Ammunition Type: High explosive (HE) with multiple warhead

===Potential operators===
*{{flag|Spain}}: Spain is currently evaluating [[K239 Chunmoo]], Astros II and [[PULS (multiple rocket launcher)|PULS]] systems, but the decision regarding a potential order of one of these systems has not been made.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.infodefensa.com/texto-diario/mostrar/4276481/sistema-israeli-puls-principal-candidato-lanzacohetes-silam-ejercito-tierra|title=El sistema israelí PULS, principal candidato para el lanzacohetes Silam del Ejército de Tierra|first=Revista Defensa|last=InfoDefensa|website=Infodefensa - Noticias de defensa, industria, seguridad, armamento, ejércitos y tecnología de la defensa}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.armyrecognition.com/defense_news_may_2023_global_security_army_industry/spanish_army_evaluates_options_for_rocket_launcher_system_design_and_development.html|title=Spanish army evaluates options for rocket launcher system design and development|website=www.armyrecognition.com}}</ref>
* {{flag|Ukraine}}: On December 4, 2022, the Brazilian media reported a Ukrainian interest in the ASTROS system, to equip the Army in the [[Russo-Ukrainian War]] efforts. The sale was blocked by the Bolsonaro administration.<ref name="Brazil-Ukraine blocked military sales">{{cite web |url=https://www.roketsan.com.tr/en/products/multi-barrel-rocket-launcher | title=Roketsan - Multi Barrel Rocket Launcher |trans-title=Roketsan - Multi Barrel Rocket Launcher |website=Roketsan Web Site |date=6 June 2026|language=en|url-status=}}</ref> A diplomatic effort by the United States to persuade the president-elect of Brazil, [[Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva]], to unblock the deal was reported on the 5th of December 2022.<ref name="Brazil-Ukraine blocked military sales"/>
